problem: EQA-v1 assumes every question has exactly one target, and its model navigates to that target and runs VQA on the last frames. Questions that need several targets and comparisons between them (e.g., 'Is the dresser in the bedroom bigger than the oven in the kitchen?') are out of scope, and an EQA-v1 agent would lose the earlier targets' observations.
motivation: Real questions often need visiting several rooms and objects and then comparing their attributes: color, size, distance, room size. This needs tighter coupling between navigation, observation selection and reasoning than the simple navigate-then-answer pipeline of EQA-v1. The work is inspired by CLEVR and Neural Module Networks, and it casts multi-target EQA as a partially observable, embodied version of compositional visual reasoning.
key_idea: The paper introduces the MT-EQA dataset and solves it with a modular agent. Each question is decomposed into sequential sub-programs (nav_room / nav_object / query / compare). Separate room and object navigators execute the navigation steps. An LSTM controller decides when each target is reached (SELECT) and stores that target's features. A compositional VQA module compares the stored target features to answer yes/no.
insight:
The ablations show that deciding which moment to extract features from is the crux.
- **SELECT timing:** On oracle shortest paths, an LSTM encoding the whole frame sequence (seq-VQA) is near random at 52.36%, while controller-SELECTed features reach 69.77%.
- **Controller features:** With oracle best views, controller LSTM hidden states beat raw CNN features, 82.88% vs 74.14%.
- **Compositional VQA:** The comparison-based cVQA beats EQA-v1-style attention VQA, 74.14% vs 60.50% (+13.64).
- **Decoupling navigation from VQA:** Using navigator hidden states for VQA (no controller) is worse, 57.40% vs 61.45%, because the navigation and QA features are different.
- **RL fine-tuning:** It makes d_Δ positive and raises accuracy from 54.44% to 61.45%.
- **Remaining gap:** Accuracy drops about 13% from imperfect SELECT and about 20% more from imperfect navigation relative to the oracle.
method: Program generator: template-based rules map each templated question into a sequence of 7 executable program types. Examples are nav_room(phrase), nav_object(phrase), query(color/size/room_size), equal_color(), and object_size / object_dist / room_size _compare. It is always accurate because questions are template-generated; it is not learned.

Navigators: separate room and object navigators with the same architecture, trained separately. Each is an LSTM taking three inputs: CNN features of a 224x224 egocentric RGB frame (encoder multi-task pretrained on RGB reconstruction, semantic segmentation and depth, as in EQA-v1), the averaged GloVe embedding of the target phrase, and the previous action embedding. Actions are turn-left 30°, turn-right 30° and forward.

Controller: an LSTM over CNN features fused with the target embedding. It predicts SELECT when the current sub-program's target is reached, which stops that navigator and advances to the next program. For objects it stores its hidden state at SELECT as the attribute cue. For rooms it has the navigator rotate 360° (12 right turns) and concatenates the panorama CNN features.

Compositional VQA (cVQA): each stored target feature is embedded into the question-attribute space (FC+ReLU). The embeddings are concatenated and passed to an FC+ReLU conditioned on the comparison operator (equal / bigger / smaller / closer / farther). It outputs a binary yes/no and supports two or three inputs.

Training: (1) joint imitation learning with loss L = L_nav (CE on shortest-path actions) + α·L_ctrl (BCE on SELECT at key best-view positions) + β·L_vqa (BCE on answer). (2) REINFORCE fine-tuning of the navigators with a dense reward from the clipped 2D distance change in [-1, 1], plus a sparse terminal reward. For objects the terminal reward is ±1.0 depending on whether IOU_T/IOU_best > 0.5; for rooms it is ±0.2 for being inside the target room.

MT-EQA dataset: 19,287 binary questions over 588 House3D/SUNCG environments, 61 object types and 8 room types. There are 6 question types comparing color, size and distance across objects in-room/cross-room, plus room size. Questions are filtered for path feasibility and for answer-entropy ≥ 0.9, so question-only baselines score near chance (≤53.74%).

setting.backbone: Multi-task pretrained CNN encoder (as in EQA-v1) + LSTM navigators/controller + FC compositional VQA, GloVe word embeddings (trained with IL then RL)
setting.training_data: MT-EQA train split: part of 19,287 template-generated questions over 588 House3D/SUNCG houses. Supervision is shortest-path actions, best-view key positions and answers; RL fine-tuning in the simulator.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (224x224); target phrase GloVe embedding; previous action
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: turn left 30°, turn right 30°, move forward (plus controller SELECT / navigator termination)
setting.privileged: The program generator is template-rule based and always correct. The agent is spawned 10 actions (~1.9 m) from one randomly chosen target. The main model uses no other privileged information; oracle variants use GT shortest paths and/or best-view positions.

The split is assumed to be the test split, based on Table 3 ('EQA (test) accuracy'); split sizes appear only in a figure. h_T is printed as a fraction (0.33) but described in the text as a percentage, so it is converted to 0-100. IOU_r_T is a mean ratio and is kept as printed. Other oracle rows are also reported: [BestView]+attn-VQA 60.50, [BestView]+cVQA 74.14, [ShortestPath]+seq-VQA 52.36, [ShortestPath]+Ctrl+cVQA 69.77.
results: The full RL-fine-tuned model Nav(RL)+Ctrl+cVQA reaches 61.45% overall accuracy on MT-EQA. That beats the controller-less Nav(RL)+cVQA (57.40%), the IL-only Nav+Ctrl+cVQA (54.44%), Nav+cVQA (53.24%) and question-only baselines (best q-NN 53.74%, 'no' 53.28%). Navigation also improves: d_T 3.60, h_T 33%, 43% of episodes terminate in the target room. Accuracy falls sharply with path length (72.22% easy vs 54.92% hard), and in-room questions are easier than cross-room ones. The oracle with GT paths and best views reaches 82.88%, showing large remaining headroom in navigation and SELECT.
limitations: The program generator is template-rule based and relies on templated questions, so there is no natural-language generalization. Answers are binary yes/no over synthetic SUNCG/House3D scenes.

Navigation remains weak (hit accuracy 33%, distance/room-size questions ≈55%), leaving a ~21-point gap to the oracle. The agent is also spawned only 10 actions from one target, which simplifies exploration.
Targets must be visited in the order they are mentioned in the question, and no learned exploration or memory/map is used.
